_comment: Phase 4 ratchet for scripts/dev-main-schema-audit.py. A handler may reference a relation with no column contract anywhere; this number may FALL, never RISE. It is a debt counter, not a target.
_why: Phase 1 cross-products every collected *COLUMNS array against every declared table, so every file in this repo declared exactly ONE table. Consequence: each Lambda's JOINed relations were audited by NOTHING. That is how `p.name` on garden_node passed a green audit, a green unit suite and a green integration run while 500-ing every seed packet detail page in prod (BUG-SEEDDETAIL500-001).
_composition: 72 of the 186 came from ONE file: household.js is byte-identical in NINETEEN directories (single sha256) -- 18 per-Lambda copies plus canonical lambda/, which Phase 4 groups separately because it groups by Path(handler).parent -- and queries locations, inventory_items, spaces, photos. 19 dirs x 4 relations = 76, minus 4 already declared in their own dir (inventory-items/inventory_items, locations/locations, members/locations, photos/photos) = 72. Cleared 2026-08-28 by copying household-columns.test.js beside all 19 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001).
_how_to_lower: Add a keyed contract to that lambda's *columns.test.js:  const AUDIT_COLUMNS = { <table>: ['col', ...] };  -- keyed pairs bind columns to ONE relation, so they do not cross-product. Then lower uncovered_relations here. See lambda/inventory-items/garden-node-columns.test.js for the worked example.
_first_lowering: 187 -> 186 on 2026-08-28 (V4-CROPTYPEALIAS-001). lambda/dashboard now declares crop_types via the keyed AUDIT_COLUMNS form in crop-types-columns.test.js — the first joined relation in the repo to carry its own contract, and the mechanism working as intended rather than a one-off.
_second_lowering: 186 -> 114 on 2026-08-28 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). household-columns.test.js declares locations, inventory_items, spaces and photos via the keyed AUDIT_COLUMNS form in all 19 household.js dirs. Two prod traps encoded there: spaces has NO deleted_at and photos has NO name, so the four arrays are deliberately not identical. Copies held byte-identical by lambda/household-columns-sync.test.js.
_third_lowering: 114 -> 104 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). garden-node-columns.test.js in the ten remaining dirs that JOIN public.garden_node: dashboard, events, facebook-share, findings, harvests, photos, preservation, projects, tags, ux-events (inventory-items and plants already declared it). NOT copies -- the column set differs per consumer, 2 columns in ux-events to 16 in events, each derived from that directory's own handlers and verified against live prod. Three of the ten reach the table with NO alias, which no alias scan can attribute, so those arms are pinned to their literal SQL and their columns listed by hand (events critterAward + give-away availability, projects deleted/active planting counts, ux-events M2 capture-week UNION).
_fourth_lowering: 104 -> 94 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). event-log-columns.test.js in the ten dirs that JOIN public.event_log without declaring it: lambda (the root group -- Phase 4 groups by Path(handler).parent, and the canonical copies of authz-parents.js and household.js live there, so lambda/ is a dir-group in its own right and PHASE1_GLOB's lambda/**/ matches at the root), daily-plan-read, dashboard, evidence-ingest, facebook-share, photos, plants, projects, ux-events, varieties. Column sets range from 1 (ux-events, one UNION arm) to 15 (dashboard's flagged-issue feed, the only reader of severity/resolved_at/title). Six of the ten share a five-column floor from authz-parents.js, byte-identical in seven dirs for the same per-directory-zip reason household.js is. Five unaliased arms pinned to literal SQL: three in plants/merge.js (dedup plan, repoint ledger, readFingerprint -- the sole reader of updated_at), the deny-by-default public project event list in projects, and the ux-events UNION arm.
_fifth_lowering: 94 -> 85 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). container-columns.test.js in the nine dirs that JOIN public.container without declaring it: dashboard, events, findings, photos, plants, preservation, projects, tags, ux-events. Range is the widest of the three relations done this session -- 2 columns in preservation and tags (pure ownership walks) to 23 of the table's 30 in projects, which is container's home directory. events is the shape worth noticing: THIRTY statements for EIGHT columns, because events joins a container to prove household ownership via created_by rather than to read project content. Eleven unaliased arms pinned to literal SQL, seven of them in projects/index.js including three near-identical list projections distinguished only by their parent_id predicate; mutation M11 breaks one pin alone to prove the three do not absorb each other.
_sixth_lowering: 85 -> 77 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). plant-projects-columns.test.js in the eight dirs that JOIN public.plant_projects without declaring it: lambda (the root group), events, evidence-ingest, harvests, photos, plants, tags, varieties. Six of the eight share the same four columns from authz-parents.js -- byte-identical in seven dirs for the same per-directory-zip reason household.js is -- whose loadOwnedProject is the ownership gate every write naming a container passes. harvests is the outlier at five: it is the only reader of archived_at, which watch-route.js uses to keep retired containers out of the ready-to-pick watch. tags is the smallest at three, because entityExists('project') selects a bare 1 and so never reads name. Seven unaliased arms pinned to literal SQL (one per authz-parents.js copy, plus the tags original the authz predicate was lifted from).
_seventh_lowering: 77 -> 69 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). plants-columns.test.js in the eight dirs that JOIN public.plants without declaring it: lambda (the root group), events, evidence-ingest, harvests, photos, plants, projects, varieties. Five of the eight carry only authz-parents.js's five-column ownership walk, which addresses the BASE table rather than the garden_node VIEW over it because that is where the ownership CHECK constraints live (authz-parents.js:35-38). The plants directory itself is the widest contract in the repo at 30 of the table's 55 columns -- merge.js reads a planting almost whole for the merge preview -- while harvests reads four. Two unaliased arms pinned to literal SQL: the container-level harvest sub-select in events/index.js, whose inner `deleted_at IS NULL` is what stops a soft-deleted planting resolving a sibling container's harvests, and merge.js readFingerprint, the only reader of updated_at.
_eighth_lowering: 69 -> 62 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). crop-types-columns.test.js in the seven dirs that JOIN public.crop_types without declaring it: events, facebook-share, harvests, plants, preservation, tags, varieties (dashboard already declared it -- V4-CROPTYPEALIAS-001, the first keyed contract in the repo). Range 2 to 7 columns. preservation reads only slug + display_name and deliberately does NOT filter deleted_at: a preservation record keeps naming its crop type after that type is retired. plants is the mirror image -- default_unit and the DTM columns, never the label. varieties is the home directory and the only reader of category/sort_order; all four of its statements are unaliased and pinned, including the collision-set read whose ABSENT deleted_at filter is the point, because slug is the PK so a soft-deleted row still occupies it. tags and varieties share crop-derive.js byte-for-byte. This table has no id column at all, which the NOT_ON_TABLE guard in each file asserts.
_ninth_lowering: 62 -> 56 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). cultivar-columns.test.js in the six dirs that JOIN public.cultivar without declaring it: dashboard, facebook-share, harvests, inventory-items, plants, preservation (varieties already declared it). cultivar is a VIEW, not a table -- pg_get_viewdef reads `SELECT id, name AS display_name, ... FROM plant_varieties` -- which makes it the closest live analogue of BUG-SEEDDETAIL500-001: the view projects 42 of the base table's 45 columns, omitting unit_weights, weight_confidence and weight_source, and renames name to display_name, so four plausible column names resolve to nothing at runtime with nothing failing at deploy time. Each file's NOT_ON_TABLE guard asserts all four. Range 2 columns (inventory-items, a packet resolving its cultivar's label) to 20 (plants, the seed-packet detail panel -- the exact surface of that incident). No unaliased reads anywhere in the six; two dirs bind the view through the alias `pv`, which is plant_varieties' usual alias, and the guard binds by what the alias is bound TO rather than by its name.
_tenth_lowering: 56 -> 52 on 2026-08-29 (OPS-SCHEMAAUDITJOIN-001). harvest-log-columns.test.js in the four dirs that JOIN public.harvest_log without declaring it: events, harvests, plants, preservation. events is the widest at 10 of the table's 15 columns and the only reader of disposition; plants reads three, the merge fingerprint's max(updated_at) arm, and reaches the rows through event_log because harvest_log HAS NO plant_id -- the FK on it is project_id, the container. preservation is the only place in the repo that proves ownership from harvest_log.created_by directly rather than through the joined event, and its one statement is unaliased and pinned. The NOT_ON_TABLE guard in each file asserts plant_id, event_date, harvest_date (an ALIAS the handlers give event_log.event_date after the timezone shift, never a column), weight (the column is weight_grams) and name.
